Summary:
- Brimstone is an adtech platform that makes auction-time personalization decisions; ultra-latency sensitive and high QPS during bid windows.
- Primary workload: short-chat style scoring + reranking candidate ads; also periodic embedding generation for cold-start.
- Business priority: reduce per-request cost without sacrificing p95 latency; would consider quantized model paths + intelligent batching for non-critical flows.

Perf requirements / targets (from CTO call 2026-03-05):
- p50/p95 target for scoring: <= 20ms / <= 80ms (256-token budget equivalent for chat/rerank).
- Sustained throughput: 1k-3k reqs/sec during peak windows per region.
- Cost sensitivity: wants to drive token-equivalent unit cost down by >= 40% vs current hosted provider.

Technical asks and evaluation scope:
- Proof-of-concept to show Dedicated pool can hit p95 SLA at target QPS with 99.9% availability during auction windows.
- Benchmark matrix requested: model families (13B / 7B), quant configs (fp16, int8 W4/W8), batching strategies (fixed microbatch vs continuous batching), and KV/prefix cache hit scenarios.
- Wants Redwood Optimize recommendations: batching windows, cache TTLs, and quantization tradeoffs by workload.
- Explicit interest in kernel/compiler differences across instance types; asked for Redwood-verified perf pins and trace examples.
